sources.title: Encyclopædia Inflationaris

evidence.text: How can hundreds of inflationary scenarios be tested efficiently against precise cosmological data while consistently accounting for reheating and avoiding unnecessary approximations beyond slow roll?

sources.title: The importance of being warm (during inflation)

evidence.text: Can a radiation bath and nontrivial inflaton occupation numbers substantially alter primordial scalar and tensor predictions even when dissipation is weak at horizon crossing, and can this make quartic chaotic inflation compatible with the Planck data used by the authors?

sources.title: Warm DBI inflation with constant sound speed

evidence.text: Would an excited inflaton thermal distribution change scalar power enough to reconcile the weak-dissipation branch with the same CMB contours?

sources.title: Dirac-Born-Infeld warm inflation realization in the strong dissipation regime

evidence.text: Can a low DBI sound speed suppress the enhancement of curvature perturbations caused by temperature-dependent dissipation, allowing observationally viable warm inflation in the strong dissipation regime?

sources.title: Inflation from a chaotic potential with a step

evidence.text: How does a step in a quadratic chaotic inflaton potential affect the curvature spectrum, scalar tilt and tensor-to-scalar ratio in cold inflation and strongly dissipative warm inflation?

sources.title: The early universe is ACT-ing warm

evidence.text: Can symmetry-protected warm little inflaton models with simple monomial potentials accommodate the paper's ACT-era scalar tilt and tensor bounds, including strong dissipation, when both fermionic and scalar dissipative channels are treated numerically?

sources.title: Encyclopædia Inflationaris

evidence.text: Match inflation to the radiation era using an effective reheating fluid and Rrad: ln Rrad = ΔNreh(3w̄reh−1)/4. Solve for the observable field value using reheating matching rather than assigning a universal ΔN*. For w̄reh=1/3, Rrad=1 and this background matching cannot distinguish reheating from radiation domination.

sources.title: The importance of being warm (during inflation)

evidence.text: For the quartic potential, the coupled slow-roll equations reduce to an equation for Q that can be integrated analytically to determine the number of e-folds. The authors additionally report numerical fluctuation evolution supporting their small-Q predictions, with details deferred.

sources.title: Warm DBI inflation with constant sound speed

evidence.text: Specify H(φ), reconstruct the DBI velocity and sound speed, calculate logarithmic derivatives, and integrate the remaining e-folds. A potential supplies H approximately when its energy dominates.

sources.title: Dirac-Born-Infeld warm inflation realization in the strong dissipation regime

evidence.text: Numerically extract G(Q*) as the ratio of spectra with and without the explicit inflaton–radiation perturbation coupling. Fit representative results with G(Q*)=1+Ac Q*^α+Bc Q*^β, with coefficients depending on c and sound speed.

sources.title: Inflation from a chaotic potential with a step

evidence.text: Warm fluctuations obey a Langevin-like equation with localized Gaussian noise. Discrete noise is G/√dt. The paper reports 500 realizations for 0.01 ≤ k/k0 ≤ 32.5 and 50 for 35 ≤ k/k0 < 100; spectra are fitted using splines of degree 5 with smoothing S = 10⁻¹⁵. Spectral indices use numerical differentiation of interpolated spectra.

sources.title: The early universe is ACT-ing warm

evidence.text: The pivot crossing time is determined by following post-inflationary evolution until effective radiation domination, w≈1/3. This gives N*=58.27 for the WLIF Q*=0.27 benchmark and N*=55.86 for the WLIS Q*=100 benchmark, replacing earlier fixed N*=60 evaluations.

sources.title: The Warm Inflation Story

evidence.text: Can interactions sustain particle production, dissipation and primordial fluctuations during inflation, with microphysics fast enough to survive expansion? The review also asks whether this dynamics improves first-principles inflation model building.

sources.title: Warm Inflation in the light of Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Additional friction can slow the inflaton on a potential whose slope would obstruct conventional cold slow roll. The dissipation ratio Q compares this friction with Hubble friction, while a radiation bath supplies thermal fluctuations during inflation.

sources.title: Warm Inflation and its Microphysical Basis

evidence.text: How can interacting quantum fields generate dissipation, radiation and stochastic inflaton fluctuations during inflation, and under what conditions do these effects support viable warm inflation?

sources.title: Warm inflation

evidence.text: Can a first-order transition sustain inflation with an approximately equilibrated thermal component, sufficient density perturbations and many e-folds, without a tiny coupling or a separate large reheating episode?

sources.title: Warm inflation model building

evidence.text: How does microphysically motivated dissipation change inflationary dynamics, primordial spectra and supersymmetric model building for monomial, hybrid and hilltop potentials? This invited review also extends earlier model analyses.

sources.title: Warm inflation solution to the eta problem

evidence.text: Can dissipation during inflation satisfy slow-roll and density-perturbation requirements with mφ≫H, η≫1 and sub-Planckian inflaton amplitudes, thereby avoiding the usual eta problem without symmetry protection of an exceptionally flat potential?

sources.title: Warm DBI inflation with constant sound speed

evidence.text: Can dissipative DBI inflation reconcile a quartic potential with CMB constraints while allowing a steep potential during slow expansion? The paper compares a cold baseline with a constant-sound-speed warm construction.

sources.title: Reheating and Dark Radiation after Fibre Inflation

evidence.text: How do perturbative inflaton decays in Fibre Inflation determine reheating temperature, CMB e-fold count and axionic dark radiation, and thereby sharpen conditional predictions for the scalar spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio?

sources.title: A new mechanism for generating density perturbations from inflation

evidence.text: Can spatial fluctuations in inflaton decay couplings generate the dominant primordial density perturbations through inhomogeneous reheating, and how would this change inflationary scale, spectral-tilt and non-Gaussianity predictions?

sources.title: Recent Developments in Warm Inflation

evidence.text: How does dissipative particle production realize warm inflation, support viable microscopic models, modify primordial perturbations, and permit compatibility with observations and swampland conjectures?

sources.title: Warm inflation as a way out of the swampland

evidence.text: Can simple phenomenological dissipation laws maintain observationally acceptable inflation at large dissipation? A constant ratio Υ/(3H) gives an analytically convenient case that differs dynamically from a constant coefficient.

sources.title: Constant roll warm inflation in high dissipative regime

evidence.text: Can constant-roll inflation be reconstructed analytically with inflaton dissipation into radiation, and can its thermal perturbations fit the historical observational constraints or exhibit super-horizon enhancement?

sources.title: Composite Dissipation in Warm Inflation: Implications for the Primordial Power Spectrum

evidence.text: Can composite dissipation sustain strongly dissipative warm inflation with a CMB-compatible red spectrum at large scales and enhanced, blue-tilted power at small scales? How sensitive are these predictions to phase durations, transition conditions, and perturbation growth fits?

sources.title: Reheating and Entropy Perturbations in Fibre Inflation

evidence.text: Does reheating in the considered one- and two-field Fibre Inflation models begin with self-resonance, and can amplified entropy fluctuations destabilize super-Hubble curvature perturbations?

sources.title: Warming up the fibres

evidence.text: Can four established fibre-inflation potentials support observationally viable warm inflation in weak and strong dissipation, and can stronger dissipation reduce field excursions while retaining perturbative control of type-IIB compactification?

sources.title: Warm inflation with Barrow holographic dark energy

evidence.text: Can Barrow holographic dark energy (BHDE), interacting with radiation, drive warm inflation in a highly dissipative regime while satisfying slow-roll conditions and the observational bounds quoted in the paper?

sources.title: Composite inflation and further refining dS swampland conjecture

evidence.text: Can four strongly interacting composite-inflaton models satisfy a combined potential-derivative conjecture while retaining acceptable scalar and tensor spectra?

sources.title: Runaway potentials in warm inflation satisfying the swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Can generalized exponential runaway potentials support strongly dissipative warm inflation with a graceful exit, observationally acceptable perturbations, and simultaneous compatibility with the distance, de Sitter, and Transplanckian Censorship conjectures?

sources.title: Towards a reliable effective field theory of inflation

evidence.text: Can a perturbative QFT model with renormalizable matter interactions sustain observationally viable inflation through strong dissipation, with a super-Hubble inflaton mass and sub-Planckian excursion, thereby addressing the usual inflaton naturalness problem?

sources.title: Does fractal universe favour warm inflation: Observational support?

evidence.text: Can a prescribed fractal spacetime measure support warm inflation in weak and strong dissipation, and can selected measure profiles and dissipation laws yield predictions inside the historical Planck 2018 scalar-index/tensor-ratio contours?

sources.title: Warm Inflation in the light of Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Can dissipation allow a single inflaton to satisfy conjectured limits on its excursion and potential slope while producing a tensor-to-scalar ratio below the observational benchmark? The paper asks how the answer changes between weak dissipation, Q < 1, and strong dissipation, Q > 1.

sources.title: Warm inflation as a way out of the swampland

evidence.text: Can a dissipating inflaton coupled to a thermal radiation bath satisfy assumed bounds on field excursion and potential slope while producing an acceptable scalar spectrum and tensor amplitude?

sources.title: Warm pseudoscalar inflation

evidence.text: Can a pseudoscalar inflaton coupled directly to light SU(2) gauge fields sustain warm inflation while avoiding dangerous thermal corrections, and produce acceptable scalar/tensor perturbations and small non-Gaussianity in a dissipative regime with f<Mp?

evidence.text: For small oscillations, approximate V by mφ²φ²/2+gφ³/6 and reduce the linear fluctuation equation to Mathieu form. evidence.text: Integrate the sourced fluid equations, use inflaton-dominated power-law expansion, and extremize the approximate radiation density. Convert density to temperature and entropy through ρr=(π²/30)gE T⁴ and s=(2π²/45)gS T³.

evidence.text: Can thermal trapping or additional inflaton damping reconcile inflation with conjectural restrictions on scalar excursions and potential derivatives, and does either mechanism evade trans-Planckian censorship?

sources.title: Axion monodromy inflation, trapping mechanisms and the swampland

evidence.text: Can energy transfer into particles sustain inflation on a steep axion potential over a Planckian or smaller excursion? The paper compares self-production of the inflaton with repeated production of additional fields and asks whether either mechanism permits an exit.
